subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Carbon Border Taxes
description: A 60-second lesson on Carbon Border Taxes.

hook.text: The EU charges a tax on imports based on their carbon content. Dirty production abroad now costs more.

buildup.text: Carbon border adjustment mechanisms (CBAMs) tax imports from countries with weaker climate rules.

discovery.text: They prevent 'carbon leakage'—companies moving production to polluting countries to dodge domestic regulations.

twist.text: CBAMs add cost and complexity to global trade. Exporters must now track and report product-level emissions.

climax.text: The EU CBAM goes live in stages from 2026. Other countries are developing similar border carbon taxes.

punchline.text: Carbon now has a price at the border. Plan accordingly.

quiz.question: What is a carbon border tax designed to prevent?
options: Carbon leakage to countries with weaker climate rules
